topic.subject: social
topic.title: Natural vegetation and wildlife
topic.scope: tropical evergreen and deciduous forests, thorn forests, mangroves, montane forests, wildlife reserves

nodes.name: Deciduous trees die in dry season
Mangroves only grow in salt water

misconceptions.statement: Evergreen trees never shed their leaves at all.
misconceptions.why: Students interpret 'evergreen' literally as 'always green' without leaf loss.
misconceptions.fix: Evergreen trees do shed leaves, but they do it at different times of the year so the forest always appears green.

probe.question: Why do evergreen forests look green throughout the year?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the trees never lose their leaves.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning
misconceptions.source_hint: science education research on plant biology

misconceptions.statement: Deciduous trees are dead during the dry season.
misconceptions.why: Students associate leaf shedding with plant death.
misconceptions.fix: Deciduous trees shed leaves to conserve water during dry periods and regrow them when moisture is available.

probe.question: What happens to deciduous trees in the dry season?
probe.wrong_answer: They die and wait for the next rain to grow back.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: All forests need the same amount of rain to grow.
misconceptions.why: Students fail to differentiate between forest types based on climate requirements.
misconceptions.fix: Different forest types have specific rainfall requirements; for example, evergreen forests need over 200cm, while thorn forests need less than 70cm.

probe.question: Do all forests require the same rainfall?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, all forests need high rainfall to survive.

misconceptions.root_belief: one event has one single cause

misconceptions.statement: Mangroves are only found in the ocean.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse coastal ecosystems with open ocean environments.
misconceptions.fix: Mangroves grow in coastal areas, deltas, and estuaries where fresh water from rivers mixes with salt water.

probe.question: Where are mangrove forests typically found?
probe.wrong_answer: Deep in the middle of the ocean.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: Tropical evergreen forests are found only in India's Western Ghats.
misconceptions.why: Textbook examples of Western Ghats and Northeast India are remembered as the only places.
misconceptions.fix: Tropical evergreen forests also grow in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Northeastern states, wherever rainfall is above 200 cm.

probe.question: Name one region other than the Western Ghats where tropical evergreen forests are found.
probe.wrong_answer: There is none, they grow only in the Western Ghats.

misconceptions.root_belief: Examples given in a textbook are the only places

misconceptions.statement: Tropical evergreen forests have only a few kinds of trees, like a plantation.
misconceptions.why: Students think dense forest means many trees of the same kind, as seen in plantations.
misconceptions.fix: Tropical evergreen forests have very many species of trees, shrubs and creepers growing in several layers, so they are very dense and varied.

probe.question: Are evergreen forests made of one or two main tree species?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, only one or two types of trees grow there.

misconceptions.statement: Deciduous trees shed their leaves because of cold winter, not because of dryness.
misconceptions.why: Students link leaf fall with autumn in cold countries.
misconceptions.fix: In monsoon (tropical deciduous) forests the trees shed leaves in the dry summer season to conserve water.

probe.question: Why do tropical deciduous trees shed their leaves?

misconceptions.root_belief: Leaf fall is always caused by cold
misconceptions.source_hint: studies on students' ideas about plants and seasons

misconceptions.statement: Thorn forests grow in areas with heavy rainfall.
misconceptions.why: Students think any forest needs a lot of rain, and confuse thorn forests with dense forests.
misconceptions.fix: Tropical thorn forests grow in dry regions with less than 70 cm of rainfall, with thorny bushes and long roots.

probe.question: Is rainfall in thorn forest regions more than 200 cm?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, they get very heavy rainfall.

misconceptions.statement: Mangrove forests are found only on the coast of West Bengal.
misconceptions.why: The Sundarbans is the only mangrove example most students remember.
misconceptions.fix: Mangroves grow in tidal areas of deltas and coasts, including the Sundarbans, Mahanadi, Godavari and Krishna deltas and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

probe.question: Which Indian delta other than the Ganga-Brahmaputra has mangroves?
probe.wrong_answer: None, only West Bengal has mangroves.

misconceptions.root_belief: One famous example is the only example

misconceptions.statement: Mountain forests have the same kind of trees at all heights.
misconceptions.why: Students picture a mountain as one forest from bottom to top.
misconceptions.fix: In montane forests the vegetation changes with height, from tropical to temperate forests, then coniferous, alpine meadows and tundra near the top.

probe.question: What type of vegetation is found near the snowline of a mountain?
probe.wrong_answer: Same dense forest as at the foot of the mountain.

misconceptions.root_belief: Vegetation is uniform across a region
misconceptions.source_hint: geography education research on altitudinal zonation

misconceptions.statement: Temperature rises as one goes higher up a mountain because it is closer to the sun.
misconceptions.why: Students reason from distance to the sun rather than from thinner air and heat from the ground.
misconceptions.fix: Temperature falls with height, about 6.5°C for every 1000 m, so higher places are cooler and have different vegetation.

probe.question: Will the top of a 3000 m mountain be warmer or colder than its base?
probe.wrong_answer: Warmer, because it is nearer to the sun.

misconceptions.source_hint: research on student ideas about seasons and temperature

misconceptions.statement: Biosphere reserves are the same as zoos, where animals are kept in cages.
misconceptions.why: Students link wildlife protection with captive animals.
misconceptions.fix: Biosphere reserves are large protected natural areas where plants, animals and local people live in natural habitats, and animals are not caged.

probe.question: How are animals kept in a biosphere reserve?
probe.wrong_answer: In cages and enclosures, like a zoo.
